source: Deng et al., The Language-Energy Divide, arXiv:2606.21869v1 (preprint, 2026-06-20)
method: Table 5 (full results for all 122 languages, Qwen3-8B on Belebele) parsed from the paper PDF. Only the rows cited by the article are frozen here; ranks are derived over all 122 rows.
license_note: The authors' companion CSV is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and is NOT redistributed here, nor is the paper text. Only the individual figures cited by the article are recorded, plus ranks derived from them. Run `python fetch_sources.py` to re-derive the full 122-language ranking from the published PDF.
measurement_caveat: Open models (Qwen3-8B, Gemma3, Llama-3.1) on an academic L40S GPU, measured by hardware counter (NVML/Zeus), not by a wall-plug meter. Absolute joules are NOT comparable to production per-prompt figures; only the ratios between languages travel.
table_1_note: Table 1 of the same paper prints 179x for Southern Pashto against English (3,146,541 J). Table 5 gives 187.8x (3,148,022.6 J against 16,762.1 J). The article uses 179x, the value the authors sign, and records the difference.
